title: User Interface
summary: Apps, page layouts, Lightning pages, buttons and actions: shape what people see and tap, on desktop and on the phone, mostly with clicks.

lessons.title: Apps, tabs and navigation
lessons.objective: Describe the user interface customization options.

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: A **Lightning app** is a named set of tabs and tools for one job, like Sales or Finance. Users switch apps in the **App Launcher**. Each app has a **navigation bar** with items such as objects (tables of data, like Account), pages and dashboards. You build apps in **App Manager** in Setup.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: A toolbox for each trade. The plumber and the electrician share one garage, but each grabs a box with the right tools. Where it stops: an app only groups things. It never decides who can see the data.

cards.title: What the app wizard sets
items: Name, logo and primary color
**Standard** or **console** navigation
Form factors: desktop, phone or both
Navigation items, in order: the top one is the landing page
A **utility bar** of always-there tools
Which **profiles** can use the app

cards.title: The utility bar
cards.body: A **utility bar** is a fixed footer in a Lightning app. It gives one-click tools such as Notes, Recent Items or a Dialer. Each tool opens in a small panel, so users never leave the record they are on.

cards.title: Custom tab types
items: **Custom object tab**: lists a custom object's records
**Web tab**: shows an outside web page
**Visualforce tab**: shows a Visualforce page
**Lightning component tab**: shows a custom Lightning component
**Lightning page tab**: adds a Lightning app page to the navigation bar

cards.title: Console navigation
cards.body: A **console app** opens each record as a **workspace tab** and related records as subtabs. Agents can juggle many records on one screen. **Standard navigation** opens one record at a time. Pick console for busy desks, like customer support.

Taking an app away from a profile hides the app, not the data. Users can still reach records through search or links. To block records, change object permissions and sharing. An app is a menu, not a lock.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: App = which toolbox. Tab = one door. Utility bar = the pocket that is always there.

terms.say: A named bundle of tabs and tools for one kind of work, like a Sales app. You pick it from the App Launcher.
The grid of squares where you pick which app to open. It lists every app you are allowed to use.
The row of items across the top of an app. Each item opens a list, a page or a dashboard.
The Setup page where admins create and edit apps.
A strip of handy tools at the bottom of an app, like Notes. Click one and it pops up without leaving your page.
A settings card for a group of users. It says what they can open and do. Every user has exactly one.
A tab that shows another website inside Salesforce. No code needed.
A tab that puts a page you built in Lightning App Builder into an app's navigation bar.
An app style that opens records as tabs side by side. Good when people handle lots of records at once.
In a console app, the main tab for one record. Related records open as smaller subtabs under it.

lessons.title: Page layouts, record types, compact layouts
lessons.objective: Describe the user interface customization options.

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: A **page layout** decides which **fields** (single facts, like Phone), buttons and related lists show on a **record** page. A record is one row of data, like one customer. The layout also sets their order and can make a field required or read-only on that layout.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: One form, printed in different versions for different teams. Same filing cabinet, different paper. Where it stops: leaving a field off the paper doesn't lock the cabinet. **Field-level security** is the lock.

cards.title: Who gets which layout
cards.body: A user's page layout comes from their **profile** plus the record's **record type**. A record type can offer different **picklist** values (the choices in a drop-down) and a different layout. For opportunities, cases, leads and solutions it also picks a **business process**, like the sales stages.

cards.title: The layout grid
cards.code:
Profile      Record type   Page layout
Sales Rep    Retail        Retail Sales Layout
Sales Rep    Wholesale     Wholesale Layout
Support      Retail        Support Layout
Support      Wholesale     Support Layout
cards.body: Each profile and record type pair gets exactly one page layout.

cards.title: Record type rules
items: The name "Master" is reserved
One record type for a profile? Users are never asked to choose
Users can still view and edit records of other record types they have access to
Professional Edition needs the Record Types add-on

cards.title: Compact layouts
cards.body: A **compact layout** picks the key fields shown at the top of a record, in the **highlights panel**. Lightning Experience shows up to the first 7. The mobile app's highlights show up to 10. Set one as the **primary compact layout**; each record type can have its own.
Removing a field from a page layout only hides it on that page. Users may still see it in reports, list views or the API. To truly hide a field, use **field-level security**.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: Profile + record type = layout. Compact layout = the headline. Field-level security = the lock.

terms.say: The plan for a record page: which fields, buttons and lists show, and in what order.
One fact on a record, like a phone number. Like one box on a paper form.
One saved item, like one customer or one order. Like one filled-in paper form.
A label that sorts records into kinds, like Retail or Wholesale. Each kind can get its own layout and drop-down choices.
A drop-down field. You pick from a set list of choices instead of typing.
The list of steps a record moves through, like sales stages. Only opportunities, cases, leads and solutions have one.
A short list of a record's most important fields. They show at the top of the record page and in the mobile app.
The box at the top of a record page that shows its key fields and buttons.
The compact layout an object uses by default, unless a record type has its own.
The real lock on a field. It decides if a user can see or edit that field anywhere: pages, reports and the API.

lessons.title: Lightning App Builder and page types
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine the declarative options available for incorporating Lightning components in an application.

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: **Lightning App Builder** is a drag-and-drop tool for **Lightning pages**. You pick a **template**, which sets the page's regions and columns. Then you drop **components** into it. A component is a ready-made building block, like a chart, a list or a set of tabs. No code needed.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: LEGO. The template is the baseplate, the components are the bricks. Where it stops: some bricks are filled from somewhere else. The **Record Detail** component still takes its fields from the page layout.

cards.title: Main page types
items: **App page**: a home page for an app, on desktop and phone. It supports only global actions
**Home page**: the Lightning Experience home, desktop only
**Record page**: the page for a record, on desktop and phone
A page's type can't be changed after you create it

cards.title: Who sees which page
cards.body: You **activate** a page to give it to users. A record page can be the **org default**, an **app default**, or assigned by app, record type and profile. You can also pick the **form factor**: desktop or phone. The most specific assignment wins.

cards.title: App Builder or page layout?
cards.body: Only Lightning pages can be assigned by app or form factor. Only they hold custom components and tabs of components. But with the Record Detail component, field placement still comes from the page layout. App Builder doesn't touch Salesforce Classic pages.
Changing a page's template or activation never moves fields inside Record Detail. Those fields come from the page layout. Edit the layout, or upgrade the page to Dynamic Forms.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: Template = the plate. Components = the bricks. Activation = who gets it. Most specific wins.

terms.say: A drag-and-drop page maker in Setup. You build pages from blocks instead of writing code.
A page built in Lightning App Builder from a template and blocks.
The page's skeleton. It decides how many regions and columns the page has.
A ready-made block you drop on a page, like a chart, a list or a set of tabs.
A block that shows a record's fields in one big chunk. The fields inside come from the page layout.
A Lightning page that is a home base for an app. It works on desktop and phone.
The first page people see in Lightning Experience on a computer. You can give different teams different ones.
The page that shows one record, like one account, with its details and related lists.
The page everyone gets when nothing more specific is set for them.
The kind of screen: a computer (desktop) or a phone.

lessons.title: Dynamic Forms and dynamic actions
lessons.objective: Given a scenario, determine the declarative options available for incorporating Lightning components in an application.

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: **Dynamic Forms** puts each field and field section on a Lightning record page as its own component. Then you can show or hide each one with a **visibility rule**. **Dynamic actions** do the same for the buttons and actions on the page.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: A smart paper form that says "skip this part if you have no car." People only see questions that apply. Where it stops: hiding a field is about tidiness, not security. **Field-level security** still decides who may read it.

cards.title: Visibility rules
cards.body: A **visibility rule** shows a component only when its filter is true. Filters can use record fields, the **user** (like their profile or role), permissions and the **device**. App and Home pages have no record, so they filter on user, permission or device only.

cards.title: Why Dynamic Forms helps
items: Place fields anywhere, across columns and tabs
Fewer page layouts and record types to manage
Create, edit and clone use the fields on the page, not the page layout
Make a field required or read-only on this page only
Works on most **LWC-enabled** objects. Events and Tasks aren't, so they keep page layouts

cards.title: Two rules
cards.code:
Field Section: Shipping Details
  Show when: Record > Status equals Shipped

Action: Approve Discount
  Show when: Record > Discount__c greater than 20
         AND User > Profile > Name equals Sales Manager
cards.body: The section and the action appear only while their rules are true.

cards.title: Dynamic actions
cards.body: Turn them on in the **Highlights Panel** component, then add actions in App Builder with filters. Users then see these actions, not the ones from the page layout. The switch applies only to that one record page.
A field set to Required in App Builder but hidden by a visibility rule can be saved empty. And a hidden field is still readable in reports and the API. Use **field-level security** to protect data.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: Dynamic Forms = fields that come and go. Dynamic actions = buttons that come and go. Visibility rule = the when.

terms.say: A way to place each field on a page as its own block, so it can appear or hide depending on the situation.
A "show only when" setting on a block. Example: show this field only when Status is Closed.
Buttons on a record page that appear only when you say so, set up in Lightning App Builder.
A group of fields under one heading on a page.
The person looking at the page. Rules can check things about them, like their profile.
What the person uses to look at the page: a computer or a phone.
Objects whose record pages are built with Salesforce's newer page technology. Dynamic Forms works on most of them.
The block at the top of a record page with key fields and the action buttons.
The real lock on a field. It decides if a user can see or edit it everywhere, not just on one page.

lessons.title: Custom buttons and links
lessons.objective: Demonstrate the capabilities and use cases for custom buttons, links, and actions.

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: A **custom button** or **custom link** sends users somewhere from a record or a list. It can open a website, a **Visualforce page**, or a web address with record data filled in. Links sit in the record's links area. Buttons sit next to the standard buttons.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: A speed-dial button with the number already saved. The **merge fields** fill in the right number for each record. Where it stops: a button is a shortcut, not a permission. Hiding it doesn't stop anyone.

cards.title: Display types
items: **Detail Page Link**: a link on a record page
**Detail Page Button**: a button on a record page
**List Button**: a button on a list view or related list. It can act on the records users tick

cards.title: What it runs
items: **URL**: opens a web address, with merge fields
**Visualforce page**: must use the **standard controller** of the same object (list buttons: the standard list controller)
**OnClick JavaScript**: Classic only. Not in Lightning Experience or the mobile app

cards.title: A URL button
cards.body: When clicked, the merge fields fill in this account's street and city.

cards.title: Replace or override
cards.body: To swap a standard button on a record page, create your custom button, then swap them on the page layout. To change a standard action like New or Edit everywhere, **override** it with a Visualforce page or Lightning component.

cards.title: In the Salesforce mobile app
cards.body: Custom links, list view buttons and OnClick JavaScript buttons don't show in the **Salesforce mobile app**. URL and Visualforce buttons on the page layout do.
Hiding the Delete button doesn't stop deleting. Users can still reach the action another way. To stop an action, remove the permission, like Delete on that object.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: Link = words. Button = box. List button = many records. JavaScript button = Classic only.

terms.say: A button an admin adds. Clicking it opens a web address or a page, often with the record's data filled in.
Like a custom button, but shown as a text link on the record.
A custom page built with Salesforce's older page language. A developer writes it.
Placeholders like {!Account.Name}. When clicked, they turn into the real values from the record.
A custom button that sits on one record's page.
A custom button on a list of records. It can work on the records you tick.
Built-in logic that lets a Visualforce page show and save one kind of record. A record button's page must use the same object's one.
An old button type that runs browser code. It works only in Salesforce Classic.
Replace a built-in action, like New, with your own page everywhere it appears.
The Salesforce app for phones and tablets.

lessons.title: Quick actions: global or object-specific
lessons.objective: Demonstrate the capabilities and use cases for custom buttons, links, and actions.

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: A **quick action** opens a small form for one fast task. It can create a record, update this record, log a call or send an email. There are two kinds: **global actions** work anywhere, and **object-specific actions** work on one object's records.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: Sticky notes. A global action is a notepad in your pocket: you can write anywhere, but the note isn't stuck to anything. An object-specific action is a note stuck right onto one folder. Where it stops: both kinds are set up once by an admin, not by each user.

cards.title: Global actions
cards.body: Global actions live on the **global publisher layout** and in the header's global actions menu. They don't know the page you are on. They can't prefill fields from it, and a record they create has no relationship to the current record.

cards.title: Object-specific actions
cards.body: These live on one object's page layout and know the record. Create a Record links the new record to it automatically. **Update a Record** edits it. **Log a Call** logs against it. Custom ones can run a flow, a Lightning component, a Visualforce page or a canvas app.

cards.title: Rules the exam loves
items: Creating a child in a **master-detail** relationship needs an object-specific action
A Visualforce object-specific action needs that object's standard controller; a global one can't use any standard controller
**Predefined field values** set defaults when the action opens
Each action has its own **action layout**: just the fields you add

cards.title: One action, set up
cards.code:
Action: New Site Visit  (object-specific, on Account)
  Type: Create a Record
  Target object: Site_Visit__c
  Action layout: Visit Date, Purpose
  Predefined value: Status = Planned
cards.body: Each new visit links to the account by itself and starts as Planned.
A global Create action can't link the new record to the record you are on. Even placed on an account page, it makes an unrelated record. If the link matters, use an object-specific action.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: Global = anywhere, knows nothing. Object-specific = right here, knows this record.

terms.say: A shortcut button that opens a small form to do one job fast, like logging a call.
Quick actions you can use from almost anywhere. They don't know which record you are looking at.
Quick actions for one kind of record. They know which record you are on and can link to it.
The special layout that holds the global actions. It isn't tied to any object.
An action that lets you change a few fields of the record you are looking at, quickly.
An action that saves a note about a phone call or meeting as a task.
A strong parent and child link between records. The child can't exist without its parent, and deleting the parent deletes the children.
Values an action fills in by itself, so users don't have to type them.
The short list of fields shown in a quick action's little form.

lessons.title: Custom Lightning components on pages
lessons.objective: Describe the programmatic customizations available for incorporating custom Lightning components in an application.

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: When no standard component does the job, a developer can build a **custom component**. Today that means **Lightning Web Components** (LWC); the older framework is **Aura**. Once it's set up, admins drag it onto pages in App Builder like any other block.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: A custom LEGO brick made in a workshop. It fits the same baseplate as the shop bricks. Where it stops: someone must make it (code), and stamp it "fits App Builder" (configuration).

cards.title: Not automatic
cards.body: A custom component doesn't appear in App Builder by itself. The developer configures it. For LWC, the component's config file sets `isExposed` to true and lists **targets**: the page types it may go on, like `lightning__RecordPage`.

cards.title: An LWC config file
cards.body: This component can go on record pages and app pages, but not on Home pages.

cards.title: Settings for admins
cards.body: A developer can add **properties** (design attributes) that admins fill in on the page, like a title or a number of rows. A component can also be limited to phone or desktop. Aura components use interfaces such as `flexipage:availableForAllPageTypes`.

cards.title: Clicks before code
cards.body: Try standard components, Dynamic Forms and **AgentExchange** components first. AgentExchange is Salesforce's marketplace, formerly AppExchange. Build a custom component only for look, logic or data no standard block gives.

Custom **container components**, like your own tabs or accordion, aren't supported in App Builder. They show on the canvas, but you can't drop anything inside. Use the standard Tabs or Accordion component.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: Expose it, target it, then drag it.

terms.say: A page block a developer writes in code, for jobs the ready-made blocks can't do.
Salesforce's modern way to build page blocks with web code. LWC for short.
Salesforce's older way to build page blocks. It still works, but new ones usually use LWC.
A setting in the component's file. When it is true, admins may use the block in App Builder.
The list of page types a component is allowed on, like record pages or app pages.
The target name that lets a component go on record pages.
Little settings a component offers, like a title. Admins fill them in on the page, no code.
A tag an Aura component wears so App Builder lets it go on any Lightning page.
Salesforce's app store. You can install ready-made apps and page blocks from it. It used to be called AppExchange.
Blocks that hold other blocks, like tabs. App Builder only lets you fill the standard ones.

lessons.title: Making it great on mobile
lessons.objective: Given a set of requirements, determine the appropriate global, object-specific actions and layouts to optimize the Salesforce mobile user experience.

cards.title: In plain words
cards.body: The **Salesforce mobile app** shows the same data on a small screen. People there want the key facts fast, with few taps. Optimizing means showing less, but the right things first.

cards.title: Think of it like…
cards.body: A pocket guidebook next to a big encyclopedia. Same facts, but the pocket book puts the useful ones up front. Where it stops: there is no separate mobile database. You only choose what shows first.

cards.title: Layout tips
items: Put the most important fields in the **compact layout**: they show in the record highlights
Use **sections**, with the most important at the top
Keep **required fields** few
Use **default values** and record types, so fewer fields show
Phones show fields in one column

cards.title: Actions on mobile
cards.body: The mobile **action bar** shows actions from the layout's "Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions" section, or from dynamic actions. Put the few that mobile users need first, like Log a Call or New Task.

cards.title: Mobile pages
cards.body: Build an **App page** in Lightning App Builder, activate it and add it to the **mobile navigation**. Good standard blocks: Report Chart, List View, Recent Items and **Launchpad**, a grid of one-tap shortcuts. Preview in App Builder, then test in the real app.

cards.title: Phone or desktop
cards.body: Lightning record pages can be assigned by **form factor**, so phones get a lighter page. A single component can also show on phones only, with a device visibility rule.
Custom links, list view buttons and JavaScript buttons don't show in the mobile app. A link desktop users love is missing on phones. Rebuild it as a URL button or a quick action.

cards.title: Remember it
cards.body: Mobile = must-see first: compact layout up top, few fields, the right actions in reach.

terms.say: The Salesforce app for phones and tablets. It shows the same data as on a computer.
A short list of a record's most important fields, shown at the top of the record.
Groups of fields under a heading, so people can jump to the part they need.
Fields that must be filled in before you can save. Fewer is easier on a phone.
A value a field fills in by itself on new records, so nobody has to type it.
The row of action buttons on a record in the mobile app, like Log a Call.
A Lightning page that works as a home base for an app, on desktop and phone.
The menu of places you can go in the mobile app.
A page block with a grid of big shortcut tiles. One tap opens each place.
The kind of screen: a computer (desktop) or a phone.

flashcards.front: How do you build a Lightning app?
flashcards.back: In Setup, open **App Manager** and click New Lightning App. The wizard sets branding, navigation style, items, utility bar and profiles.

flashcards.front: Which custom tab shows an outside website?
flashcards.back: A **web tab**. It shows an external web page inside Salesforce, no code needed.

flashcards.front: When do you pick console navigation?
flashcards.back: When users juggle many records at once, like a support desk. Records open as workspace tabs with subtabs.

flashcards.front: Does hiding an app stop users from seeing its records?
flashcards.back: No. An app is a menu. Data access comes from object permissions and sharing.

flashcards.front: What decides which page layout a user sees?
flashcards.back: Their **profile** plus the record's **record type**. Each pair maps to one layout.

flashcards.front: What does a compact layout control?
flashcards.back: The key fields at the top of a record. Lightning Experience shows up to the first 7. The mobile highlights show up to 10.

flashcards.front: Which objects get a business process on their record types?
flashcards.back: Opportunity (sales process), Case (support process), Lead (lead process) and Solution (solution process).

flashcards.front: How do you truly hide a field from some users?
flashcards.back: Use **field-level security**. Removing it from a layout only hides it on that page.

flashcards.front: Can you change a Lightning page's type later?
flashcards.back: No. A page's type is fixed. Create a new page of the right type.

flashcards.front: How can a Lightning record page be assigned?
flashcards.back: As the org default, an app default, or by app, record type and profile. You can also pick desktop or phone. Most specific wins.

flashcards.front: Where do fields in the Record Detail component come from?
flashcards.back: From the object's **page layout**. Edit the layout, or upgrade the page to Dynamic Forms.

flashcards.front: What do Dynamic Forms give you?
flashcards.back: Each field and section as its own component, with **visibility rules**. Fewer page layouts, one assignment model.

flashcards.front: What can a visibility rule filter on?
flashcards.back: Record fields, the user, permissions and the device. App and Home pages have no record, so no record filters.

flashcards.front: Where do you turn on dynamic actions?
flashcards.back: In Lightning App Builder, on the **Highlights Panel** component of that record page.

flashcards.front: Which custom button types don't show in the mobile app?
flashcards.back: Custom links, list view buttons and OnClick JavaScript buttons. URL and Visualforce buttons on the layout do show.

flashcards.front: What must a Visualforce page use to be a detail page button?
flashcards.back: The **standard controller** of the same object. A list button page uses the standard list controller.

flashcards.front: Does hiding a standard button stop the action?
flashcards.back: No. Users can still reach it another way. Remove the permission instead.

flashcards.front: What replaces OnClick JavaScript buttons in Lightning Experience?
flashcards.back: Quick actions, such as a flow or Lightning component action, or a URL button.

flashcards.front: Global or object-specific: which links a new record to the current one?
flashcards.back: **Object-specific.** A global create action makes a record with no relationship to the page you are on.

flashcards.front: How do you create a master-detail child with an action?
flashcards.back: With an **object-specific** action on the parent. Global actions can't create detail records.

flashcards.front: What are predefined field values?
flashcards.back: Defaults an action fills in when it opens, like Status = Planned.

flashcards.front: Where do Lightning and mobile actions come from on a page layout?
flashcards.back: The "Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions" section. Not customized? They come from the global publisher layout.

flashcards.front: How does a custom LWC appear in Lightning App Builder?
flashcards.back: Its config file sets `isExposed` to true and lists **targets**, like `lightning__RecordPage`.

flashcards.front: How do admins set options on a custom component?
flashcards.back: Through **properties** (design attributes) the developer adds. Admins fill them in App Builder.

flashcards.front: Are custom tab or accordion components supported in App Builder?
flashcards.back: No. Custom containers show, but you can't drop components into them. Use the standard Tabs or Accordion.

flashcards.front: What goes in the compact layout for mobile users?
flashcards.back: The most important fields. They show in the record highlights, up to 10 on mobile.

flashcards.front: How do you build a mobile home page?
flashcards.back: Create an **App page** in Lightning App Builder, activate it, and add it to the mobile navigation.

flashcards.front: How can phone users get a lighter record page?
flashcards.back: Assign a lighter Lightning record page to the phone form factor. Or hide some components on phones with a device visibility rule.

questions.q: The finance team at Larkspur Foods wants its own set of tabs, its own logo, and a Notes tool that is always one click away at the bottom of the screen. What should the app builder create?
options: A Home page in Lightning App Builder for the finance profile
A permission set that grants the finance tabs and a Notes field
A Lightning app in App Manager with a utility bar
A record page with a Rich Text component and a list of links
questions.explain: A Lightning app bundles tabs, branding and a utility bar. You build it in App Manager, and the utility bar adds the Notes tool as a fixed footer.
wrong: A Home page is one page. It doesn't bring its own tabs, logo or utility bar.
A permission set grants access. It doesn't build a branded app or a footer tool.
A record page belongs to one object. It can't set the app's tabs or logo.

questions.q: Brightwave Travel wants its partner booking website to open inside Salesforce from the navigation bar. Nobody on the team writes code. Which tab type fits?
options: A web tab
A Visualforce tab
A custom object tab
A Lightning component tab
questions.explain: Web tabs show any outside web page inside Salesforce. They need no code.
wrong: A Visualforce tab needs a Visualforce page, which someone must code.
A custom object tab lists records of a custom object, not a website.
A Lightning component tab needs a custom component, which is code.

questions.q: Agents at Harbor Health handle many cases at once. They want to open a case, then its contact, without losing the case they started on. Which app setting meets this need?
options: Use standard navigation and add a utility bar
Add the Contact tab to the top of the navigation items
Assign a separate Lightning app to each support profile
Use console navigation in the Lightning app
questions.explain: Console navigation opens records as workspace tabs, with related records as subtabs. Agents can keep the case open while they look at the contact.
wrong: Standard navigation opens one record at a time, even with a utility bar.
Tab order doesn't keep several records open side by side.
More apps don't change how records open inside an app.

questions.q: An app builder adds a new Lightning app page called Today's Jobs to the Field Service app. Technicians must land on that page every time they open the app. What should the app builder do?
options: Set Today's Jobs as the org default Home page
Move Today's Jobs to the top of the app's navigation items
Add Today's Jobs to the app's utility bar as the first item
Mark the page as the default in each technician's profile
questions.explain: The item at the top of an app's navigation list is its landing page, on desktop and mobile.
wrong: Today's Jobs is an app page, not a Home page. App pages aren't assigned as Home pages.
The utility bar is a footer of tools. It doesn't set the landing page.
Profiles don't pick an app's landing page. The order of items does.

questions.q: Which two can an app builder set in the New Lightning App wizard? (Choose 2)
options: Field-level security for the fields shown in the app
A utility bar with tools like Notes and Recent Items
The org-wide default sharing for the app's objects
The user profiles that can use the app
The record types users must choose for each object
questions.explain: The wizard sets branding, navigation style, form factors, navigation items, the utility bar and the assigned profiles. It never changes data access.
wrong: Field-level security is set on profiles and permission sets, not in an app.
Sharing settings are separate from apps. An app never changes record access.
Record types are assigned through profiles and permission sets, not apps.

questions.q: At Pinecrest Realty, an app builder removed the Sales app from the Contractor profile shown here. Contractors still open opportunities from global search. They must have no access to opportunities. What should the app builder do?
questions.code:

  Object settings: Opportunity  Read: yes  Edit: no

options: Also remove the Opportunities tab from every other app contractors can open

Create a second Sales app without opportunities and assign it to contractors

questions.q: Users of the Operations app shown here say they can't add or reorder their own items in the navigation bar. What explains this?
questions.code:
Operations app (Lightning app)
  Navigation style: Standard
  Default navigation items: 55
  Utility bar: Notes, Recent Items
  Assigned profiles: Operations User
options: Console apps never let users personalize navigation items
Personalization needs the Customize Application permission
Navigation items only allow personal changes on the phone app
With more than 50 default navigation items, users can't personalize the bar

wrong: This app uses standard navigation, and the cause is the item count.
Users don't need an admin permission to personalize the navigation bar.
Desktop users can personalize too, as long as the app has 50 or fewer default items.

questions.q: An app builder at Cobalt Labs built a Lightning app page in Lightning App Builder. It must appear as an item in the Lab app's navigation bar on desktop and phone. Which tab type does this use?
options: A Lightning page tab
A Lightning component tab
A web tab pointing at the page's URL
A Visualforce tab that embeds the page
questions.explain: Lightning page tabs add Lightning app pages to the navigation bar of Lightning Experience and the mobile app. Activating an app page in App Builder sets one up for you.
wrong: That tab type shows one custom component, not a page built in App Builder.
A web tab shows an outside web page, not a Lightning app page.
A Visualforce tab shows a Visualforce page, which needs code.

questions.q: Renewal deals and new-business deals at Tidewater Supply need different Stage values and different fields on the page. What should the app builder use?
options: Two page layouts assigned to the same profile
A dependent picklist that filters Stage by deal type
Two record types, each with its own sales process and layout
A validation rule that blocks the wrong Stage value for each type of deal
questions.explain: Record types give one object different picklist values, business processes and page layouts. On opportunities, the business process is the sales process with its stages.
wrong: A profile gets one layout per record type, and layouts can't change Stage values.
This wouldn't change which fields show on the page.
A validation rule blocks saves. It doesn't change the choices or the layout.

questions.q: Users want Account Number and Rating at the top of every account record, in the highlights panel. What should the app builder edit?
options: The account's page layout
The account's search layout
The account's compact layout
The account list view filters
questions.explain: The compact layout picks the fields in a record's highlights panel. In Lightning Experience, up to the first 7 show there.
wrong: The page layout controls the details area, not the highlights panel fields.
Search layouts set the columns in search results.
List views show lists of records, not the top of one record.

questions.q: An app builder set this compact layout. Desktop users don't see Open House or Lockbox Code in the highlights panel, but mobile users see all 9 fields. Why?
questions.code:
Primary compact layout: Property__c
  1 Name          6 Agent
  2 Address       7 List Date
  3 Price         8 Open House
  4 Status        9 Lockbox Code
  5 Bedrooms
options: Lightning Experience highlights show up to the first 7 fields
The compact layout needs a record type before all fields show on desktop
Desktop highlights panels show only fields that are also on the page layout
Field-level security hides the extra fields from desktop users
questions.explain: In Lightning Experience the highlights panel shows up to the first 7 compact layout fields. The mobile app's highlights show up to 10.
wrong: Record types are optional. The desktop limit is the first 7 fields.
The highlights panel reads the compact layout, not the page layout.
Field-level security is the same on every device, so mobile would hide them too.

questions.q: Support agents at Meadowlark Insurance must never see the Claim Reserve field on claims, including in reports. What should the app builder do?
options: Remove the field from every page layout that support agents use
Hide the field with a visibility rule on the claim record page
Move the field into a collapsed section at the bottom of the layout
Remove read access with field-level security
questions.explain: Field-level security decides if a user can see a field anywhere: pages, reports, list views and the API. Layouts and visibility rules only tidy one page.
wrong: A layout only hides the field on that page. Reports and the API still show it.
A visibility rule only hides it on that page. Reports still show it.
A collapsed section still shows the field to anyone who opens it.

questions.q: When creating a new record type, which two objects ask the app builder to pick a business process? (Choose 2)
options: Opportunity
Account
Case
Contact
A custom object
questions.explain: Only opportunity, case, lead and solution record types use a business process. Opportunities have sales processes and cases have support processes.
wrong: Account record types don't have a business process.
Contact record types don't have a business process.
Custom object record types don't have a business process.

questions.q: Installation work orders and repair work orders at Northgate need different key fields at the top of the record. Both use record types. What should the app builder do?
options: Create one compact layout per profile and assign it on the profile
Create two compact layouts and assign one to each record type
Set both compact layouts as primary on the object
Put all key fields in one compact layout and hide some by record type
questions.explain: Each record type can have its own compact layout, which overrides the object's primary one. Each record type gets only one.
wrong: Compact layouts are assigned to record types, not to profiles.
An object has only one primary compact layout.
Compact layouts have no rules to hide fields by record type.

questions.q: At Quill Books, the Sales Rep profile has only the Retail account record type available. Which two statements are true for sales reps? (Choose 2)
options: They can't open any Wholesale account, even ones they own
The Retail record type also limits which accounts they can see
They aren't asked to pick a record type when creating accounts
They must choose Retail from a list each time they create an account
They can still view and edit Wholesale accounts they have access to
questions.explain: If a profile has only one record type, users are never asked to choose. Record types don't control access, so users can still work on records of other types they can see.
wrong: Record types don't block access. Users can view and edit other record types they have access to.
Sharing settings decide record access, not record types.
With one record type available, users aren't prompted to choose.

questions.q: A Sales Manager opens a Wholesale account. A Sales Rep opens a Retail account. Which page layouts do they see?
questions.code:
Page layout assignment: Account

Profile        Retail              Wholesale
Sales Rep      Retail Sales        Wholesale Sales

options: Retail Sales for both, because the manager shares the rep's layout
Manager Wholesale for the manager, Retail Sales for the rep
Wholesale Sales for the manager, Retail Sales for the rep
Support Basic for both, because it is the first layout in the list
questions.explain: The page layout comes from the user's profile plus the record's record type. Read the row for the profile and the column for the record type.
wrong: The manager is opening a Wholesale record, so the Wholesale column applies.
Wholesale Sales is the Sales Rep row. The manager's row says Manager Wholesale.
Order doesn't matter. Each profile and record type pair has its own layout.

questions.q: Retail users must fill in Store Region when they edit accounts on the Retail layout. Nightly data loads through the API create accounts without that value and must keep working. What should the app builder do?
options: Make Store Region a required field in its field settings
Add a validation rule that requires Store Region for all users
Add Store Region to the Retail compact layout
Mark Store Region as required on the Retail page layout
questions.explain: Required on a page layout applies only when users edit with that layout. Required on the field itself, or a validation rule, also applies to the API.
wrong: A field that is required everywhere would make the API loads fail.
A validation rule also runs for API loads, so they would fail.
A compact layout only shows fields. It can't make one required.
questions.source: Require Field Input to Ensure Data Quality

questions.q: Sales managers at Ridgeway want one page that shows a pipeline report chart and a list of open deals, opened from the Sales app's navigation bar. There is no budget for code. What should the app builder create?
options: An App page in Lightning App Builder
A Visualforce tab with a chart
A record page for the Opportunity object
A custom report type with a chart
questions.explain: An App page is a Lightning page that works as a home base in an app. Drag in the Report Chart and List View components, then add it to the navigation.
wrong: Visualforce needs code, and standard components can already do this.
A record page shows one record, not a team overview.
A report type defines report data. It doesn't build a page.

questions.q: Sales Reps at Fernhill must get one opportunity record page, and Sales Managers another, but only in the Sales app. Other apps keep the current page. How should the app builder assign the new pages?
options: Set each page as the org default for its profile
Assign each page in the profile's page layout settings
Assign them by app, record type and profile
Set each page as the app default for the Sales app
questions.explain: Lightning record pages can be assigned by app, record type and profile. That is the most specific level, so it wins over app and org defaults.
wrong: The org default applies to everyone, not to one profile.
Page layout assignment chooses layouts, not Lightning pages.
An app default goes to everyone in the app, not one profile.

questions.q: An app builder created a Lightning Home page by mistake. It should have been a record page for accounts. What should the app builder do?
options: Change the page type in the page properties
Change the template to a record page template
Create a new record page for accounts
Activate the Home page on the account object
questions.explain: A Lightning page's type is fixed when you create it. To get a record page, make a new one.
wrong: A Lightning page's type can't be changed after it is created.
Templates set the layout of regions. They don't change the page type.
A Home page can't be assigned to an object.

questions.q: Field technicians at Brightline should get a simpler work order record page on phones, while desktop users keep the full page. What should the app builder use?
options: A Lightning record page assigned to phones
A separate page layout assigned to a mobile profile
A compact layout with fewer fields
A second record type for mobile work orders
questions.explain: Only Lightning pages can be assigned by form factor. Activate one page for desktop and another for phone.
wrong: Page layouts are assigned by profile and record type, never by device.
A compact layout changes the highlights, not the whole page.
Record types sort records, not devices.
questions.source: Deciding When to Use Lightning App Builder or the Page Layout Editor

questions.q: A Lightning record page for Invoice__c shows fields with the Record Detail component. The app builder wants to reorder those fields. Which two options work? (Choose 2)
options: Edit the invoice page layout that the users are assigned
Switch the page to a template with more columns
Activate the page again with a phone form factor
Upgrade the page to Dynamic Forms and arrange the fields in App Builder
Edit the invoice compact layout
questions.explain: Fields inside Record Detail come from the page layout. To arrange fields in App Builder instead, upgrade the page to Dynamic Forms.
wrong: A new template moves components, not the fields inside Record Detail.
Activation decides who sees the page, not the field order.
The compact layout sets the highlights panel, not Record Detail.
questions.source: Deciding When to Use Lightning App Builder or the Page Layout Editor

questions.q: A Sales Rep opens a Wholesale account in the Sales app. Which page does the rep see?
questions.code:
Account record page activations
  Org default:            Account Basic
  App default (Sales):    Account Sales
  App, record type, profile:
    Sales app + Retail + Sales Rep -> Account Retail Rep
options: Account Retail Rep
Account Basic
The system default account page
Account Sales
questions.explain: The most specific assignment that matches wins. No rule matches Wholesale, so the Sales app default applies.
wrong: That assignment is only for Retail records. This account is Wholesale.
The Sales app has its own default, which is more specific than the org default.
Custom pages are assigned here, so the system default isn't used.

questions.q: An app builder wants to add the object-specific action Update Status to a Lightning App page for the warehouse team. What happens?
options: It works once the action is added to the page layout
It can't: App pages support only global actions
It works if the page is activated for the phone form factor
It works after Dynamic Forms is turned on for the page
questions.explain: App pages aren't tied to a record, so they support only global actions. Object-specific actions need a record page.
wrong: App pages have no object, so they don't use object page layouts.
Form factor doesn't change which actions an App page supports.
Dynamic Forms is for record pages. App pages still take only global actions.

questions.q: Mobile users at Sunpath ask for a custom Lightning Home page in the Salesforce mobile app, like the one desktop users have. What should the app builder tell them?
options: Activate the Home page for the phone form factor in Lightning App Builder
Home pages are desktop only; use an App page in mobile navigation
Assign the Home page to the mobile app by profile
Copy the Home page into a record page for the User object
questions.explain: Lightning Home pages work in Lightning Experience only. For phones, build an App page and add it to the mobile navigation.
wrong: Lightning Home pages aren't available in the mobile app.
Home pages can be assigned by app and profile, but only in Lightning Experience.
A record page shows one record, so it isn't a home base.

questions.q: The Cancellation Reason field on orders should only show when Status equals Cancelled. What should the app builder use?
options: A record type for cancelled orders
A validation rule on the Status field
A separate page layout section for cancellations
Dynamic Forms with a field visibility rule
questions.explain: Dynamic Forms makes each field its own component. A visibility rule then shows it only when Status equals Cancelled.
wrong: Record types need users to switch type. They don't react to Status.
A validation rule blocks bad saves. It doesn't show or hide fields.
A layout section always shows. It can't react to Status.
questions.source: Break Up Your Record Details with Dynamic Forms

questions.q: Which feature meets this requirement for the Quote__c record page?

Requirement: Approve Discount action on Quote__c records
  Show it only when:
    Discount__c is greater than 20
    AND the user's profile is Sales Manager
options: Dynamic actions with visibility filters on the action
A page layout for managers that includes the action
A validation rule that blocks other users from approving
A global action on the global publisher layout
questions.explain: Dynamic actions let you add actions in App Builder and filter them by record fields, user and device.
wrong: A layout can't check the discount value.
A validation rule can't hide an action from the page.
Global actions don't know the record, so they can't check its discount.
questions.source: Create Dynamic Actions in Lightning App Builder

questions.q: Clearwater Bank has 6 case page layouts that differ only by a few fields for each region. The app builder wants fewer layouts to maintain. What is the best option?
options: One record type per region, each with its own page layout
One compact layout per region
One Dynamic Forms page with visibility rules
One permission set per region that hides the extra fields
questions.explain: Dynamic Forms with visibility rules reduces the number of page layouts and record types you need.
wrong: This keeps several layouts and adds record types too.
Compact layouts set the highlights panel, not the record details.
Permission sets grant access. Using them to tidy pages is the wrong tool.
questions.source: Break Up Your Record Details with Dynamic Forms

questions.q: On a Lightning App page, which two filters can a component visibility rule use? (Choose 2)
options: Fields of the current record
Fields of the current user
The record type of the current record
Fields of the record's parent account
The device form factor
questions.explain: App and Home pages aren't tied to an object, so visibility filters use the user, permissions or the device.
wrong: App pages aren't tied to a record, so there is no record to filter on.
An App page has no current record.
An App page has no record, so it has no parent either.

questions.q: An app builder hides the Salary__c field from interns with a visibility rule on the Dynamic Forms page. Interns still see salaries in a report. Why?
options: Reports ignore visibility rules unless the report is in a public folder
The rule needs the device filter set to desktop
Visibility rules don't change field-level security
The field must also be removed from the compact layout
questions.explain: Visibility rules tidy one page; they don't secure data. Remove read access with field-level security to hide it everywhere.
wrong: Report folders control who sees the report, not field access.
Device has nothing to do with reports.
A compact layout is another page part. Reports don't use it.

questions.q: On a Dynamic Forms page, Region is set to Required in App Builder. A visibility rule hides Region for partner users. Partners now save records with Region empty. Why?
options: A field hidden by a visibility rule at run time can be saved empty
Partner users skip all Required settings made in App Builder
Required in App Builder only works on records created by the API
The field needs to be required on the page layout too
questions.explain: If a field set to Required is hidden by a visibility rule, users can save without it. Make the field universally required or use a validation rule if it must always be filled.
wrong: There is no partner exception. Hidden fields simply aren't checked.
Required in App Builder is a page setting. It doesn't apply to the API at all.
Dynamic Forms pages use the page's fields, not the layout's.

questions.q: At which step does the Return Details section first appear, and why?
questions.code:
Field Section: Return Details
  Show when: Record > Status equals Returned

Step 1: user clicks Edit (Status = Shipped)
Step 2: user changes Status to Returned
Step 3: user clicks Save
options: At step 2, because visibility rules react as soon as a field value changes
At step 1, because edit mode shows every section whatever its rule says
Never, because Status filters can't be used on field sections at all
After step 3, because section rules are checked only after a save
questions.explain: Visibility rules on single fields react while the user edits. Rules on field sections are evaluated only after the record is saved.
wrong: Only rules on single fields react while editing. Section rules wait for the save.

Status is a supported filter field for sections.

questions.q: This visibility filter isn't supported. Why?
questions.code:

Show when:
  Record.Account.Owner.Manager.Manager.Manager.LastName
  equals "Ortiz"
options: Visibility filters can't use fields from related objects
The filter crosses six relationship spans, and filters allow at most five
Text fields aren't supported in visibility filters
Case record pages can only filter on the user, not the record

wrong: Related object fields are allowed, up to five spans.
Text fields are a supported filter type.
Record pages can filter on record and related fields.

questions.q: An app builder enables dynamic actions on the Account Sales record page and filters the actions there. Users on the Account Service record page still see the page layout's actions. Why?
options: Dynamic actions need a page layout change before they apply
Enabling dynamic actions applies only to the record page being edited
Service users need a permission set to see dynamic actions
Dynamic actions work only on custom objects, not on Account
questions.explain: When you enable dynamic actions, it applies only to the record page you're working on. Repeat it on the Account Service page.
wrong: Once on, the page uses its own actions, not the layout's.
No special permission is needed to see dynamic actions.
Dynamic actions work for standard and custom objects.
questions.source: Create Dynamic Actions in Lightning App Builder

questions.q: An app builder opens the Event record page in Lightning App Builder and finds no Fields tab to drag fields from. What is the best next step?
options: Turn on Dynamic Forms on Mobile in Salesforce Mobile App setup
Switch the page to a custom template that supports Dynamic Forms
Create a record type so the Fields tab appears
Manage event fields in the page layout instead
questions.explain: Dynamic Forms isn't supported on objects that aren't LWC-enabled, like Events and Tasks. Their record pages use the page layout.
wrong: That setting is for mobile. Events still don't support Dynamic Forms.
Custom templates don't add Dynamic Forms for unsupported objects.
Record types don't turn on Dynamic Forms.
questions.source: Break Up Your Record Details with Dynamic Forms

questions.q: Reps want a button on account pages that opens a mapping website for that account's billing address. What should the app builder create?
options: A custom detail page button with a URL and merge fields
A global quick action that creates a map record
A list button on the Accounts list view that opens the map site
A web tab that points at the mapping website
questions.explain: A URL custom button can use merge fields like `{!Account.BillingCity}`, which fill in the record's values when clicked.
wrong: A global action doesn't know which account is open.
A list button acts on a list, not one record's address.
A web tab can't fill in the account's address.

questions.q: Managers at Oakmont want to tick several leads in a list view and send them all to a review page at once. Which custom button setup fits?
options: A Detail Page Button on the lead page layout
A Detail Page Link in the lead layout's Custom Links section
A List Button with Display Checkboxes selected
A List Button with Display Checkboxes cleared
questions.explain: List Buttons appear on list views and related lists. Select Display Checkboxes when users must pick individual records.
wrong: A detail page button works on one record at a time.
A link on a record page can't act on records ticked in a list.
Without checkboxes, users can't select individual records.

questions.q: Aspen Logistics is moving to Lightning Experience. Several OnClick JavaScript buttons stopped showing. What should the app builder do?

Move the buttons to the page layout's Custom Links section
Rebuild them as quick actions, such as flow or Lightning component actions
Add the buttons to the compact layout of each object
questions.explain: OnClick JavaScript buttons work only in Salesforce Classic. In Lightning Experience, replace them with quick actions or other supported options.
wrong: No such setting exists. JavaScript buttons aren't supported in Lightning.
Moving them doesn't change the unsupported button type.
Compact layouts hold fields, not buttons.

questions.q: Interns at Galeworks must not delete opportunities. The app builder already removed the Delete button from their page layout, yet an intern still deleted one. What should the app builder do?
options: Remove the Delete permission on Opportunity for interns
Also remove Delete from the opportunity compact layout
Override the Delete button with a blank Visualforce page
Add a validation rule that blocks deletes by interns
questions.explain: Hiding a button removes it from one page, but users can still reach the action. Take away the permission to really stop it.
wrong: Compact layouts hold fields. Actions there don't control permissions.
An override is a workaround, not security. Users may find other ways.
Validation rules run on save, not on delete.

questions.q: An app builder wants a link to the company's policy page shown in the links area of every case record. Which display type fits?

Detail Page Button
Web tab
Detail Page Link
questions.explain: A Detail Page Link is a custom link shown on the record page. Detail Page Buttons and List Buttons are buttons.
wrong: A list button goes on lists, not on a record's links area.

A web tab is a navigation item, not part of the record page.

questions.q: Which two custom buttons and links on a page layout appear for users in the Salesforce mobile app? (Choose 2)
options: A detail page button with a URL content source
A detail page link that opens a website
A list button on the Accounts list view
A detail page button that runs OnClick JavaScript
A detail page button that opens a Visualforce page
questions.explain: In the mobile app, URL and Visualforce buttons from the page layout show. Custom links, list view buttons and JavaScript buttons don't.
wrong: Custom links aren't available in the mobile app.
List view buttons aren't available in the mobile app.
JavaScript buttons aren't supported in the mobile app.

questions.q: A developer wrote this Visualforce page to print labels for Shipment__c records. The app builder wants a detail page button on Shipment__c that opens it, but the page isn't in the content list. Why?

</apex:page>

A detail page button's page must use the standard controller of Shipment__c
Visualforce pages can be used only as list buttons, not detail buttons
The page must be added to a Visualforce tab before it can be a button
questions.explain: Visualforce pages used as detail page buttons or links must use the standard controller of the same object. This page uses Account.
wrong: It is the other way round: the object's standard controller is required.
Visualforce pages work as detail buttons when the controller matches.
A tab isn't needed. The controller is the problem.

questions.q: Whenever a user clicks New on Project__c, from the tab, a list view or a related list, they must see a custom guided page. What should the app builder do?

Override the standard New action on Project__c with a Lightning component
Hide the New button on every Project__c list view
Add a global action named New Project to the publisher layout
questions.explain: Overriding a standard action replaces it everywhere it appears. Swapping buttons on a page layout only changes that layout's buttons.
wrong: Layout buttons appear on one record page. New appears on tabs and lists.
Hiding New stops nothing and shows no new page.
The standard New button would still open the old page.

questions.q: Reps at Saltmarsh want to log a Site Visit from an account page, and each visit must link to that account automatically. What should the app builder create?
options: A global Create a Record action for Site Visit
A custom list button on the Site Visit list view
A web tab that opens the Site Visit page
An object-specific Create a Record action on Account
questions.explain: Object-specific create actions know the record you're on. The new record is linked to it automatically.

questions.q: Employees at Kestrel Media want to create an Expense record from anywhere in Salesforce. The expense isn't tied to any other record. What should the app builder create?

An object-specific action on Account
A custom detail page button
A Lightning record page for Expense
questions.explain: Global actions work from almost anywhere and create records with no relationship to other records. That fits a stand-alone expense.
wrong: This only appears on account pages, and expenses aren't tied to accounts.

A record page shows an existing expense. It doesn't create one from anywhere.

questions.q: What should the app builder add to this action to meet the requirement?

  Requirement: Status must start as Planned,

A predefined field value for Status on the action
Status as the first field in the compact layout
questions.explain: Predefined field values fill in fields when a quick action runs. Users don't have to type them.

questions.q: Which two statements about object-specific actions are true? (Choose 2)

questions.q: An app builder set up this action. Reps notice the new contacts aren't linked to the account they were viewing. Why?

  Target object: Contact
  Placed on: Account page layout (Mobile and Lightning actions)

Global actions only link records in the mobile app

Global actions don't link records on any device.

questions.q: An app builder wants users to add invoice lines with a quick action. What should the app builder do?

questions.explain: Actions that create a detail record in a master-detail relationship must be object-specific, not global. Put the action on the master, Invoice__c.

Layout placement doesn't matter. The object can't be a global target.
Permissions don't make the object available to global actions.

questions.q: A developer built this page to use as a global custom action that works from anywhere, with no specific record. The action can't be created with this page. What must change?

<apex:page standardController="Account">
  <!-- address lookup: map, local time, weather -->
</apex:page>
options: The page must use the standard controller of User
The page must use a standard list controller instead

questions.q: Service leads at Lumen Dairy want to select 50 cases in a list view and change them in one step. Which two quick action types can be used as mass quick actions? (Choose 2)

Lightning Web Component

questions.q: Silverbirch's account page layout has two Create a Record actions for opportunities: New Deal and New Renewal. New Renewal is set to the Renewal record type. Sales reps have no access to that record type. What do reps see?
options: Only New Deal
Both actions; New Renewal saves with their default record type
Both actions; New Renewal fails when they save
Neither action until the record type access is fixed

wrong: The action doesn't switch record types. It's hidden instead.
Reps never get the action, so they never reach an error.
Only the action tied to the missing record type is hidden.

questions.q: A user clicks this action on a case. What does the Priority field show, and can the user change it?

Action: Escalate (on Case, Create a Record: Escalation__c)
  Action layout: Reason, Priority
  Priority field default value: Medium
  Predefined field value on the action: Priority = High

Medium, because the field's default value wins
High, locked so the user can't change it
Blank, because the two values clash
questions.explain: When a field has both a predefined value and a default value, the action uses the predefined value. If the field stays on the action layout, that value shows as a default the user can change.
wrong: The predefined value beats the field's default value.
A predefined value on a field that's on the layout can still be changed.
Nothing is blanked. The predefined value wins.

wrong: `lightning__RecordPage` is for record pages in Lightning App Builder.

Change `actionType` to `Action`

questions.q: An app builder at Nettlefield plans to rebuild the two-column account layout as one column, just for phone users. What is the best advice?

Move every field into the compact layout instead
Skip it; the mobile app shows fields in one column anyway
Turn off the second column in Salesforce Mobile App Setup

wrong: Layouts follow profiles, not devices, and the app already shows one column.
The compact layout is for a few key fields, not every field.
There's no such setting. The app arranges the columns itself.
questions.source: Tips for Optimizing Page Layouts for the Salesforce Mobile App

questions.q: On a record page, a Quick Scan component has the visibility filter Device equals Phone. A rep opens the record in the Salesforce mobile app on a tablet, then in a web browser on the same tablet. Where does the component appear?

In the browser only
In both views
In neither, because a tablet isn't a phone
questions.explain: The Salesforce mobile app on a tablet uses the phone form factor. A browser on a tablet uses the desktop form factor, so the component shows only in the app.
wrong: A browser on a tablet counts as desktop, so the phone filter hides it there.
The browser view uses the desktop form factor.
The mobile app on a tablet uses the phone form factor.

The app's primary color and logo settings

Branding doesn't affect where the app appears.
